thread:
Clare: heads up — validator_score spike on prod for fncall flows around 06:10 UTC, ~4.2% of calls flagged as schema_mismatch. looks like a noisy false-positive pattern.
Ken: can you paste an example payload? curious if it's strict enum mismatch or trailing whitespace stuff.
Clare: pasted a sanitized example, see below:
Clare: ```json
{
  "tool": "price_lookup",
  "result": {
    "items": [
      {"id": "sku:123", "price": "$12.00"}
    ],
    "meta": {}
  }
}
```
Sam: aha — price is a string with a dollar sign, validator expects number. that will trip strict schema validation.
Tori: did we not have a soft-validate flag for tool responses? should've been castable and allowed through with a warning.
Ken: current rollout of strict tool validation (canary) turned on for 10% of traffic last night; looks like these flows hit the canary slice.
Clare: right. My concern is telemetry: dashboard shows a big spike under "structured_rejects" which triggered quota alarms for some customers. noisy alerts.
infra-bot: deploy 2173334600 starting canary slice rollback for service 'tool-adapter' — reason: schema-reject spike.
deploy-bot: canary rollback succeeded at 2173334601 :white_check_mark:
Sam: proposal: add a 'relaxed_tool_validator' path for adapters where we coerce common types (strip $, parse ints) and emit a 'validator_score' tag with reason code.
Tori: agree. also add a scoreboard metric: `validator_reject_reason` with top-k sampling so console can show dominant causes without exploding cardinality.
Ken: for immediate mitigation we should back off strict canary to 1% and mark affected customers as 'soft-validate' until we deploy coercions. can we do that with routing policy toggles?
Clare: yes, routing policy supports per-customer override; I can flip the canary slice for the main tenant. will do + post update.
Clare: done — Canary slice reduced to 1% for strict-validation group. monitoring in grafana.
Sam: next steps: (1) add coercion helpers in tool-adapter lib (2) emit `validator_reason` tag + `coerce_applied=true/false` (3) dashboard: add top-5 reasons and a small per-route heatmap (4) rollout: staged canary with e2e prompt tests.
Tori: +1. UX note: Console should annotate when a route has 'soft-validate' vs 'strict-validate' so customers know why some calls are blocked.
Ken: telemetry change: store reason as a low-cardinality enum and also sample full reason strings at 1% to S3 for debugging.
Clare: will draft a short ops playbook for on-call: how to triage validator spikes, how to flip routing override, and when to rollback canary.
Sam: I'll open a PR for adapter coercions and a small feature flag to enable per-route coercion.
Tori: can we also add an incidentbot hook to suppress quota alerts when `coerce_applied=true` spikes happen? otherwise on-call gets paged.
Clare: good call. we'll add a suppression rule tied to metric tags, not just absolute thresholds.
Ken: timeline: PRs today, small canary tomorrow, dashboard widgets next week. anyone blocking?
Sam: no blockers, I'll start now.
Tori: I'll sketch the dashboard mock and update console annotation copy.
Clare: thanks all. I'll follow up with the ops playbook and add a short blurb in the release notes about "relaxed tool validation".
Ken: appreciate it. :thumbsup:
Clare: closing loop — will post final postmortem if the pattern persists.
